name: Orecchiette
notes: The little “ears” are Puglia's signature pasta. Look for them with bitter greens, anchovy and toasted breadcrumbs.

name: Focaccia barese
notes: Thick but airy, baked with tomatoes, olives and plenty of olive oil; the crisp, oily base is the best part.

name: Pasticciotto
notes: A warm oval of shortcrust pastry filled with custard. It began in nearby Galatina and is best eaten at breakfast.

name: Puccia salentina
notes: A wood-fired bread pocket with a crisp shell, filled to order with vegetables, cheese, meats or tuna.

name: Fritto misto
notes: A paper cone or platter of lightly fried local fish, squid and prawns—ideal after a long saltwater day.

name: Burrata
notes: Invented in Puglia: a mozzarella pouch enclosing creamy stracciatella. Seek it out very fresh and simply dressed.

name: Rustico leccese
notes: Flaky puff pastry hiding béchamel, tomato and mozzarella—a humble, molten Salento institution.

name: Caffè leccese
notes: Espresso poured over ice and sweetened with almond syrup: practically designed for a Puglian August afternoon.
